info.name: Resource-resolution matrix (attribute-rich pre-authorization, Phase 5.97)
info.description: Proves the 00-DESIGN §3 behavior matrix live through APISIX: with the catalog service's AbacResourceResolver registered, an id'd @OpaPreAuthorize decision is made on the RESOLVED instance (tags + ancestors) with the role looked up once on the governing root — the team/tag model finally governs id'd writes. Cells: the headline flip (E1), the closed realm-fallback hole (E2), the intended narrowing (E3), the unchanged non-member fallback (E4), hierarchy parity via the gate (E5), the T5 product-policy sibling (E6), and the pinned missing-id 403 posture. Fixture set: the dedicated 8888… catalog pair seeded by run-resource-resolution-matrix.sh.

item.name: E1. THE HEADLINE FLIP: viewer-realm member, tag-gated write role, PUT the emea Category -> 200 (pre-5.97: 403)

exec: pm.test('E1: the tag-matched write is ALLOWED at the gate (story C4) -> 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('E1: the handler ran on the authorized snapshot (name updated)', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().name).to.eql('EMEA root (updated by the gated writer)'); });

item.name: E2. THE HOLE CLOSES: editor-realm member, same tag-gated role, PUT the apac Category -> 403 (pre-5.97: 200 via the tag-blind fallback)

exec: pm.test('E2: the realm role no longer leaks a write the team role\'s tags deny -> 403', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });
pm.test('E2: problem+json ACCESS_DENIED (a gate deny, not an error)', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().errorCode).to.eql('ACCESS_DENIED'); });

item.name: E3. THE NARROWING: read-only team role + editor realm, PUT -> 403 (role definition present, fallback disabled)

exec: pm.test('E3: a present role definition disables the realm fallback -> 403', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });

item.name: E4. NON-MEMBER UNCHANGED: editor realm, PUT a Category in the team-less catalog -> 200 (the fallback still decides)

exec: pm.test('E4: no role definition at the root -> the realm fallback decides, byte-identical -> 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.name: E5. HIERARCHY PARITY: root-granted member GETs a nested Category -> 200 VIA THE GATE (inherited grant survives the move from layer 3)

exec: pm.test('E5: a catalog-root read grant authorizes the nested category AT THE GATE -> 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
pm.test('E5: the response is the resolved snapshot', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().id).to.eql(pm.variables.get('nested_category_id')); });

item.name: E6a. THE PRODUCT SIBLING (T5 live): tag-gated writer PUTs the apac Product -> 403 (the ported conjunct denies)

exec: pm.test('E6a: product.rego now carries tags_satisfied -> the apac product write denies -> 403', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });

item.name: E6b. THE PRODUCT SIBLING, allow half: the same writer PUTs the emea Product -> 200

exec: pm.test('E6b: the emea product write satisfies the conjunct -> 200', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

item.name: 7. PINNED SEMANTIC: a missing id behind an annotated resourceId -> 403, not 404 (resolver empty => gate deny)

exec: pm.test('missing id -> 403 (anti-enumeration; pre-5.97 this was 404)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(403); });
